step1_analysis.circuit_type: Differential to Single-Ended Clock Buffer / Receiver
step1_analysis.description: Converts a differential input clock signal into a single-ended rail-to-rail clock. It consists of a differential amplifier with a current mirror active load, followed by a CMOS inverter stage to sharpen the edges and provide full swing.

paper_reference.title: A 2.4-GHz RF Sampling Receiver Front-End in 0.18-um CMOS

propagation_delay.description: Time delay between the input clock edge and the corresponding output clock edge.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the RC time constant of the differential pair output node (N1) and the inverter delay. With ~500uA tail current and small parasitic capacitances, delay is typically around 50-150ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard delay for a two-stage high-speed buffer in 130nm at 1GHz.

rise_time.description: Time taken for the output clock to transition from 20% to 80% of VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: Inverter driving a 10fF load. I_drive ~ 1mA. dt = C * dV / I = 10f * 1.08V / 1mA = 10.8ps. Adding intrinsic parasitics, ~30ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Fast edges are required for a 1GHz+ clock to minimize jitter in RF sampling.

fall_time.description: Time taken for the output clock to transition from 80% to 20% of VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: Similar to rise time, NMOS pull-down is slightly stronger or equal depending on sizing.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Symmetric rise/fall times are ideal for clock buffers to maintain duty cycle.

duty_cycle.description: Ratio of the high time to the total period of the output clock.

sky130_expected.calculation: Ideally 50% if the differential pair is perfectly balanced and the inverter threshold is at VDD/2.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Critical for RF sampling circuits which often rely on precise clock phases.

power_consumption.description: Total power consumed by the buffer from the VDD supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: Static power: I_bias (100uA) + I_tail (500uA) = 600uA -> 1.08mW. Dynamic power: f * C * V^2 = 1G * 20f * 1.8^2 = 0.06mW. Total ~ 1.2mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by the static current of the differential amplifier.

clock_jitter.description: Variation in the timing of the clock edges.

sky130_expected.calculation: Thermal noise of the diff pair and inverter translated to timing jitter. Jitter = V_noise / Slew_rate.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected to be in the sub-picosecond range to support high-frequency RF sampling as reported in the paper.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure clock buffer delay, rise/fall times, duty cycle, and power consumption at 1 GHz.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Differential to Single-Ended Clock Buffer
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_bias=2u L_bias=0.15u
.param W_tail=10u L_tail=0.15u
.param W_dp=10u L_dp=0.15u
.param W_pm=10u L_pm=0.15u
.param W_invp=10u L_invp=0.15u
.param W_invn=5u L_invn=0.15u

I1 VDD N0 100u
XM2 N4 N4 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=W_pm l=L_pm
XM8 clk N1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=W_invn l=L_invn
XM3 N1 N4 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=W_pm l=L_pm
XM7 clk N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=W_invp l=L_invp
XM4 N4 clk_inN N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=W_dp l=L_dp
XM1 N0 N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=W_bias l=L_bias
XM6 N3 N0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=W_tail l=L_tail
XM5 N1 clk_inP N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=W_dp l=L_dp

Cload clk GND 10f

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VclkP clk_inP 0 DC 0.9 SINE(0.9 0.4 1G 0 0 0)
VclkN clk_inN 0 DC 0.9 SINE(0.9 0.4 1G 0 0 180)

.control
tran 10p 5n
meas tran v_max max v(clk)
meas tran v_min min v(clk)
meas tran t_rise trig v(clk) val=0.36 rise=2 targ v(clk) val=1.44 rise=2
meas tran t_fall trig v(clk) val=1.44 fall=2 targ v(clk) val=0.36 fall=2
meas tran t_delay trig v(clk_inP) val=0.9 rise=2 targ v(clk) val=0.9 rise=2
meas tran t_period trig v(clk) val=0.9 rise=2 targ v(clk) val=0.9 rise=3
meas tran t_high trig v(clk) val=0.9 rise=2 targ v(clk) val=0.9 fall=2
let duty_cycle = t_high / t_period
print duty_cycle
meas tran pwr_avg avg i(VVDD)
let power_mW = -pwr_avg * 1.8 * 1000
print power_mW
quit
.endc
